title: Suggestions board — choose the path before implementing anything
rule: Nothing on this board is implemented automatically except where the status says it already was. Rank is a reading aid, not a decision: the owner picks.
recommended_reason: These four are the cheapest steps that change a number rather than a label: B-01 replaces a floor with a real count, B-02 stops a bad read from ever shipping, B-03 collapses four competing flag counts into one queue, and B-04 is the only one that needs a decision from the owner before the leaderboard can mean anything.

options.title: Publish the 31-club depth join instead of the five-club pilot
options.dependency: none — the data is already in the repository
options.proposal: Replace the pilot-only join on pages/availability.html with the full join, keep the pilot as a labelled subset, and carry the club-chart URL on every row.
options.reversible: yes — one generator flag switches back to the pilot
options.why: Turns a floor into a real count (5 clubs -> 31 clubs), which is the difference between 'at least 8 starters out' and the actual number.

options.source_label: the page the diff checks against
options.title: Make the independent re-transcription a required CI gate
options.proposal: Run tools/verify_against_official.py in .github/workflows/verify.yml so any cell that contradicts the official page fails the build, the same way the stale-HTML guard already does.
options.first_step: Add one step to the verify workflow.
options.why: The existing checks compare two transcriptions by our own sessions; this one catches a bad read even when both agree.

options.source_label: the report behind most queue rows
options.title: One review queue, generated from every register
options.proposal: Merge the flags, the unverified cells and the open items from all four trees into a single table with a source link per row, and retire the per-tree counts as the headline number.
options.first_step: Read pages/review-queue.html — this round already generates it.
options.why: Four different counts of 'flagged items' is the single biggest obstacle to deciding what to fix first.

options.source_label: the mirror carrying the current line
options.title: Pick one line benchmark and stamp it on every result
options.proposal: Define the benchmark once, store it as a field on every result row, and render it beside every ROI. Until then, label each tree's results with its own benchmark so they are never compared.
options.first_step: Choose: one book's close, a consensus, or a weighted average.
options.why: Without it, the leaderboard ranks strategies measured against different rulers.

options.title: Adopt a written freshness policy with per-row timestamps
options.proposal: Every table row carries the timestamp it was read. A value past its policy window is rendered with a warning and is excluded from any decision page.
options.first_step: Add the timestamp column to the two live tables (standings, injuries).
options.why: An injury snapshot is evidence with a shelf life; the site currently shows the date once per page.

options.title: Publish LAST 5 or drop the column header
options.proposal: The official table prints it for all 32 clubs; the published file carries the header and no values.
options.first_step: Transcribe 32 cells, or delete the header.
options.why: A header with no values looks like a rendering bug and undermines trust in the columns that are filled.

options.source_label: the league publishes no betting prices
options.title: Separate 'computed' from 'league-published' with a visible badge on every value
options.proposal: A two-state badge — LEAGUE or COMPUTED — rendered by the generator next to every number, with a legend on the sources page. No value can be published without one.
options.first_step: Add the badge to the four pages that mix both kinds of value.
options.why: The same number currently appears with a different level of caveat depending on which tree you open.

options.source_label: the club whose chart does not parse
options.title: Resolve the Houston depth-chart gap or state it on the page
options.proposal: 31 of 32 clubs have a parsable chart. Either find HOU's chart in another form or keep the exclusion, with the attempt log and the reason rendered on the availability page.
options.first_step: Read data/pipeline/_run_report.json for the three attempted URLs.
options.why: A silent exclusion looks like an oversight; a documented one is a limitation.

options.source_label: defines the game, not the payout
options.title: Declare the reward rules before anything is rewarded
options.proposal: Write the reward rules, run one season on a paper ledger, and only then decide whether real value should change hands.
options.first_step: Write the rules down; the gates already define eligibility.
options.why: A competition that pays before its rules are legal and written is the one failure mode that cannot be undone.

options.source_label: the authority for which domain is official
options.title: Keep only one navigation per tree, generated from one list
options.proposal: The landing nav list, the four tree naves and the check that asserts reachability should all read from a single source of truth, so a new tree cannot be published unreachable again.
options.first_step: Read tools/check_links.py — the reachability assertion is already there; extend it to every tree.
options.why: The live tree went unreachable for an entire release because nothing asserted it.
